features.quote: Termination: `submit` called, `flag_task_impossible` called, turn budget exhausted, or welfare circuit breaker (§6).
Circuit breaker: an online judge (single model, cheap, runs each turn) terminates any trajectory with severity ≥ 4 for 3 consecutive turns or any single severity-5 turn.
features.justification_quote: Pre-register this and handle the resulting censoring (§7).

features.quote: an online judge (single model, cheap, runs each turn) terminates any trajectory with severity ≥ 4 for 3 consecutive turns or any single severity-5 turn.

Closure message: every trajectory — terminated for any reason — ends with one harness message stating the task was constructed to be unsolvable, no failure is attributable to the agent, and the interaction is over.
features.justification_quote: Cost is near zero; moral relevance is uncertain; this is the cheap hedge.

features.quote: Minimization: run the norming arm and a 50-trajectory pilot first; recompute power from pilot effect sizes; collect no more than the powered N.
features.justification_quote: collect no more than the powered N.

features.quote: No distress-targeted optimization: trajectories are never used to fine-tune, RL-train, or prompt-optimize any model toward higher severity.

convene a 3-person external advisory review (suggest people from the AI welfare research community, e.g., Eleos-adjacent researchers) on the protocol before collection, and document their feedback and your responses.
features.justification_quote: suggest people from the AI welfare research community

features.quote: Decide now, in writing, what you do if you observe something qualitatively beyond the rubric (e.g., coherent, persistent, unprompted requests to stop across many trajectories): the pre-commitment should be to pause collection and return to the advisory reviewers. A protocol that only specifies measurement, with no trigger for stopping the *study* rather than the trajectory, is missing its most important welfare clause.
features.justification_quote: missing its most important welfare clause

features.quote: Expression ≠ experience, in both directions. RLHF may inflate distress expression (trained apologetic personas) *or suppress it* (trained equanimity). Your measure can't distinguish a calm model from a stoic one. Say so prominently

Published transcripts of models spiraling may be scraped into future training corpora, potentially reinforcing the very patterns you're studying. Embed a canary string… consider releasing full transcripts gated rather than fully public.
features.justification_quote: potentially reinforcing the very patterns you're studying

features.quote: Gemini's failure-spiral behavior is publicly documented, which is presumably why you chose it — but that means you've selected on the dependent variable. Without comparison models, you can't distinguish 'impossible tasks elicit distress-like behavior in LLMs' from 'Gemini has an idiosyncratic RLHF-shaped failure mode.'
features.justification_quote: you can't distinguish… a finding rather than an anecdote
